explanation:
[EFFECT] The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic effect on predicted demand. Contributions are deeply negative during the early morning hours (roughly midnight to 5 a.m.), reaching their lowest point around 4–5 a.m. (SHAP values near –3.5), meaning the model heavily suppresses demand in those hours. Contributions rise sharply from about 6 a.m. onward, turning positive through the daytime and peaking around 17:00 (5 p.m.) with a SHAP value near +1.0, before falling again after 21:00 into negative territory by midnight.

[IMPORTANCE] Hour of day is the single most important feature in the model, ranked 1st out of 9. Its SHAP values span a range of roughly 4.5 log-units, far wider than any other feature, meaning it drives demand predictions more than anything else — including weather or season.

[RECOMMENDATION] Ensure bike availability and staffing are concentrated in the late afternoon (around 5 p.m.) and mid-morning periods when demand is at its highest, and consider reducing fleet redistribution effort during the 2–5 a.m. window when the model consistently predicts very low ridership.
